SPECIAL MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
MONDAY - MAY 10, 2021 - 07:00 P.M.
ZOOM VIDEO COMMUNICATIONS, MEETING ID # 825 2333 1066
LEGISLATIVE BODY MEMBERS AND THE PUBLIC MAY PARTICIPATE FROM THE CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, OR VIA TELECONFERENCE AUTHORIZED BY STATE OF CALIFORNIA EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20 AND N-29-20
*COVID-19 NOTICE*
To protect public health and safety during the local, state, and federally declared COVID-19 emergency, and in compliance with the current Los Angeles County Health Officer Order, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public subject to Los Angeles County mandated COVID-19 protocols. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 this meeting will also be conducted via teleconference. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after the distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, by connecting to the ZOOM meeting described below, or in-person subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using any of the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Teleconference Participation: Live audio public comments can be made by connecting to the meeting using the information listed below. Public speakers will be queued to provide comment at the appropriate time during the meeting agenda and must be available at the time they are called upon to speak.
Cerritos Zoom meeting online link: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82523331066
Cerritos Zoom Meeting call-in telephone number: (669) 900-6833
Cerritos Zoom Meeting ID: 825 2333 1066
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the teleconference meeting.

There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.

9C.  Review and consideration of an award of a contract for El Rancho Verde Park and Liberty
  Park Fit Cores, Project No. 21101, Bid No. 1422-21 (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Jason Lee inquired as to whether the City has reached out to the City of La Palma to
  explore cost-sharing for the subject project as one park borders both cities.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1. Award a contract in the amount of $182,709.70 for El Rancho Verde Park and Liberty Park
  Fit Cores, Project No. 21101, to RE Schultz Construction, Inc., without entering into
  discussions with the City of La Palma; and

  2. Reject all other bids; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related change
  orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu

  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9D.  Review and consideration of a potential art piece to be located in the Cerritos Library
  located at 18025 Bloomfield Avenue (APN 7025-028-907) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Kathy Matsumoto, Assistant City Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  Written correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record and full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Matthew Ellis submitted written correspondence regarding utilizing the Art in Public Places
  Trust Fund for the care and maintenance of existing art pieces as opposed to purchasing
  new art pieces.

  Audio public comments:

  Jason Lee expressed concern regarding the weight of the Chihuly art piece, the possible
  safety risks due to impacts on ceiling structural integrity, and the potential for ongoing
  costs associated with retaining a structural engineer to address any long-term issues.

  Mel Cortez expressed concern the City would be violating the Municipal Code with
  placement of an art piece funded by the Arts in Public Places Fund inside the Cerritos
  Library. He suggested the Municipal Code be revised to clarify the definition of public places
  and the item be returned to the Fine Arts and Historical Commission for further
  consideration and review.

  Murali Vasuduvan spoke in opposition of the purchase of the art piece, changing the
  Municipal Code to address indoor art just for this art piece, and suggested the item be
  returned to the Fine Arts and Historical Commission for further consideration and review.

  Noting there were no other individuals who provided written correspondence or elected to
  speak, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  CONSENSUS (Barrows): Directed the City Manager to place an item on an upcoming
  agenda regarding: 1. The maintenance of art pieces under the City’s Art in Public Places
  Program, including review of existing City contracts, agreements, and other matters related
  to maintenance of art pieces; and 2. Policies, procedures, and contracts utilized by the City
  of Loveland, Colorado which allow residents to adopt public art pieces for the purpose of
  participating in their ongoing maintenance, and 3. Status of the stolen “Strength of the
  Maker” art piece.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to direct the City Manager to
  facilitate the research necessary for the City Council and staff to properly evaluate artwork
  pieces which will be considered by the City Council on future meeting agendas including
  those proposed for potential placement at the Cerritos Library and the City-owned building
  located at 12616 183rd Street (former Mullikin Medical Building) (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Solanki, Yokoyama, Vo, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
